instrument.note: Ranks classes against each other on one shot spec. Not comparable to a route parity.json tasteReview, whose shotsHash differs; a lane re-scores on this instrument to beat the table mark and writes the receipt per TASTE.md.

rows.beats: No win named in the shot. LoopNet's Central Oregon commercial/investment search and a Bend commercial brokerage's own investment-listings page (e.g. Compass Commercial Real Estate Advisors) both open with live inventory, filters, or a map in the first screen. This page's captured viewport is two paragraphs of prose with no count, listing, chart, or map visible, so no metric win is demonstrated by what was shot — whatever wins the page (unified MLS breadth across multi-family/commercial/land/farm/business, per the route file) sits below the fold and is not judged here.

defects.finding: The entire visible viewport at both breakpoints is two prose blocks (heading + paragraph) separated by hairlines with no figure, image, map, or interactive element in sight — the page's stated 'live counts' never appear on screen.
defects.fix: Give the first Quiet item a figure slot (e.g. one hero stat — active income-property count) so the first viewport carries a number beside the claim, not prose alone.

defects.finding: Both prose items reserve a wide right-hand column — roughly the right 45% of the 1120px content width on desktop — that renders completely empty because 'prose'-kind items carry no figure; it reads as an unfinished card, not restraint.
defects.fix: When a Quiet item is prose-only, collapse the row to a single measure (44rem) instead of splitting a figure column that has nothing to fill.

defects.finding: Two consecutive items inside the section repeat the identical eyebrow-less heading-over-body-over-hairline shape back to back, and the route composes the next two sections (#market, #searches) as the same figure-row-then-ledger pattern — the stacked-section page the canon names as a failure.
defects.fix: Vary the second #place item's form — a small callout, an inline calculator teaser, or a single figure — instead of repeating the same prose row shape used by the first item.

defects.finding: The item terms 'What this page is' and 'How to underwrite here' read as documentation headers describing the page to itself, not a claim a visitor came for — it reads like a README shipped to the public rather than the quiet-editorial register.
defects.fix: Replace the meta-labels with a stated finding a person would want, e.g. a headline naming the actual number or verdict ('Central Oregon does not cash-flow at today's rates — here is what the math shows') instead of a label about the page itself.

defects.finding: Nothing in the first viewport can be hovered, toggled, scrubbed, or tapped for more data, and no figure of any kind is visible — the page's own stated job ('here is the inventory, here is the math') is answered nowhere on screen.
defects.fix: Move or duplicate one live figure (active income-property count) into the #place hero itself so the page's core promise is visible without a scroll, ahead of the Instrument section that currently carries it alone.

rows.dullest: #place — the only section in view. Two memo-style paragraphs with a void beside each and a hairline rule at the bottom; nothing in the first screen states a number, shows an image, or gives a reason to keep scrolling, so no, this is not a screen anyone stops on.
tells: Walls of text. — #place: two paragraph blocks with no figure, image, map, or interactive element
The stacked-section page. — #place's two items repeat the same eyebrow-less heading/body/hairline shape, and the route composes #market → #searches as the same figure-row-then-ledger pattern next
rows.verdict: This is a cover memo, not a landing page — a headline and two internal-sounding paragraphs with an empty box beside each, no number, no listing, and nothing to touch anywhere in the first screen, which trips the wall-of-text and stacked-section rules directly regardless of what the Instrument and Ledger sections do once a visitor scrolls past it.

rows.beats: No win named for what the shots show. Redfin's and Zillow's saved-homes/compare screens render the visitor's own saved thumbnails on first view; this page's empty state shows a sentence and a link instead. The richer populated feature set the route file describes (photo compare, best-in-class highlighting, map, PDF, share link) is not represented in these shots and cannot be credited here.

defects.finding: The entire visible page (desktop and mobile alike) is a heading, one two-sentence paragraph, and a text link — no illustration of what a finished four-home comparison looks like, no sample rows, no thumbnails, nothing to look at that explains the product before the visitor commits effort to finding and adding homes.
defects.fix: Replace the prose-plus-link block with a composed preview — four visible comparison slots (empty card outlines or faint sample rows behind an overlay) that show the shape of the output, not just describe it in a sentence.

defects.finding: Zero interaction anywhere in the first viewport: no hover, scrub, or toggle. TASTE.md requires every data section to reward interaction with more data; here there is no data section at all when unpopulated, only static text — the 'up to four' claim has no visual slot counter a visitor can watch fill.
defects.fix: Give the four-slot limit a visual form (four outlined tiles) so adding a home from another tab or a recent-view rail is something the visitor can see happening, not a number stated in prose.

defects.finding: This is the single most generic empty-state pattern available — heading, sentence, link — indistinguishable from any SaaS empty-cart screen. Nothing on the page itself (only the inherited nav, footer, and Amboqia H1 from shared chrome) says Central Oregon or Ryan Realty; no deliberate choice was made for this page's job.
defects.fix: Compose the empty state as a first-class object: a thin navy diagram of the comparison table's four columns with placeholder rows, or thumbnails of the visitor's two or three most recently viewed listings offered as one-tap adds — show the product, don't narrate it.

defects.finding: No preview of the populated state exists anywhere on this page, so the page's own promised job — compare up to four homes side by side with photos, feature table, best-in-class, map, PDF, share link (per the route file's own description) — is not demonstrated in the one screen most visitors will ever see if they never add four homes.
defects.fix: Surface a static example of the populated comparison (blurred/sample data, clearly labeled) so the honest function of the tool is visible even to a visitor who arrives with zero homes queued.

rows.dullest: The whole first viewport, both desktop and mobile — "Up to four homes" plus one sentence plus a text link is the entire page above the footer; nothing rewards scrolling because there is nothing below it. A visitor would not stop scrolling here because there is nothing past the first two lines to read.
rows.verdict: The compare tool's landing state is an empty form label, not a product demo — it should show the comparison, not describe it, and right now it does neither.

rows.beats: No win named. The fold's only content is a hairline-divided directory list (thumbnail, name, one-line description, right-aligned count) — the same shape Zillow's and Redfin's state/city-list pages use, and those use larger, consistently-present card photography plus stat chips where this page has small, inconsistently-present thumbnails and bare right-aligned text. This page does not clear that baseline, let alone beat it.

defects.finding: Past the hero, the entire visible page is a hairline-divided list of rows — thumbnail, name, one-line description, right-aligned figure. This is TASTE.md's named tell verbatim: 'A Ledger past six rows with no visual encoding (no mark, no bar, no map, no image) is a table wearing hairlines.' The row does carry an `encode='bar'` prop in code, but nothing resembling a bar, a fill, or any proportional mark is visible in either shot — a reader cannot see at a glance that Bend (661 for sale) dwarfs Camp Sherman (5 for sale); they have to read every number.
defects.fix: Give each row an actual visible mark — a horizontal bar or dot sized to the shared inventory scale, drawn behind or beside the row — so magnitude reads instantly instead of requiring the reader to parse every right-aligned number.

defects.finding: Nothing in the visible fold rewards a hover, tap, scrub, or toggle with more data. Every row is a static link to another page; there is no way to compare two cities, see a trend, or reveal anything without leaving the page.
defects.fix: Make hover (desktop) / tap-and-hold (mobile) on a row reveal something the row's static text doesn't show — e.g. the city's months-of-supply verdict or a 12-month sales sparkline — so the list rewards interrogation instead of only navigation.

defects.finding: Thumbnails appear for some rows (Bend, Crooked River Ranch, Culver, Madras) and are simply absent for others (Black Butte Ranch, Camp Sherman, La Pine), producing uneven row heights and a ragged left edge down the list — reads as an unfinished data pull, not a deliberate rhythm.
defects.primitive: app/cities/page.tsx (mediaSrc: city.hero.verified ? city.hero.src : undefined, feeding V3Ledger's media slot)
defects.fix: Give every row the same media treatment — a photo for all, or a consistent navy glyph placeholder for all — never a silent mix of 'sometimes an image' within one list.

defects.finding: Every single row repeats the label 'OREGON' (7 times in the desktop fold, and it pushes onto its own line above every row on mobile) — a fact already established by the page title and never in question, occupying space that could hold real per-row data and adding to the wall-of-text feel on 375px.
defects.primitive: app/cities/page.tsx (when: v3Text('Oregon') passed into every V3Ledger row)
defects.fix: Drop the redundant per-row state label and replace it with real data the reader would use — the city's months-of-supply verdict or the snapshot's refreshed date — or remove the slot entirely.

defects.finding: The regional claim ('1,571 homes for sale... Balanced market at 4.9 months of supply') is stated as a plain sentence with no mark next to it — exactly the pattern TASTE.md's MOS guidance warns against ('MOS is two bars... not a tile that says 3.9'). The number is accurate to the formula and thresholds, but it ships as prose, not a graphic.
defects.fix: Render the months-of-supply claim as the two-bar form (active listings vs. a month of sales) instead of a sentence, so the region's headline claim has a mark before the list even starts.

rows.dullest: The city list itself: seven-plus hairline-divided rows of a thumbnail, a name, a one-line description, and a bare right-aligned number — the literal "wall of text, scrolling lists" Matt named, with no bar, chart, map, or interaction anywhere in the fold.
tells: Scrolling lists as the design — the entire visible page below the hero is a hairline-divided directory list with no visual encoding of magnitude (thumbnails are present/absent inconsistently and carry no data; the count column is bare right-aligned text), matching TASTE.md's 'table wearing hairlines' definition exactly.
rows.verdict: Fails the gate. Median score 30/100, well below any passing bar, on a page whose entire visible content is the one pattern TASTE.md names first as the problem: a scrolling, hairline-divided directory list with no chart, no map, no bar, and nothing to hover, scrub, or toggle. The hero headline is properly on-brand (Amboqia, navy-on-cream, correct months-of-supply math and verdict), so honesty/function and basic craft hold up reasonably, but design quality and originality — the two 30-point criteria this rubric weights hardest — collapse because nothing below the headline was composed as an object; it's a stack of text rows. The primitive at fault is shared: components/site/v3/V3Ledger.tsx, used for the whole visible section, so the fix (a real bar/dot encoding, a hover reveal, consistent media, dropping the redundant per-row 'OREGON' label) raises every page that calls V3Ledger this way, not just /cities.

rows.beats: No win named. The visible viewport is a plain photo/price/badge/address card grid — the same form as Redfin's "price reduced" filtered search results or a Zillow price-cut list — with no chart, sparkline, or hover-reveal beyond it, and it is additionally broken by an overlapping signup card that a competitor's page does not have. Cannot claim a win on depth, interactivity, or even legibility against either.

defects.section: Get new Central Oregon listings by email (id="alerts", PriceDropAlertsSheet)
defects.finding: The email-capture card renders on top of the second listing card instead of in normal flow: its heading, input field, and "Get alerts" button sit directly over the listing's photo, price, address, and disclaimer text, so both the CTA and the listing beneath it are illegible. On mobile the overlap is total — "New Listings" overlaps "$3,750,000", the email form overlaps the second photo, and the -12.0% badge peeks out from under the "Get alerts" button.
defects.fix: Give the alerts card its own row in the grid's normal document flow (or a full-width band between grid rows) instead of a position that pulls it up over a sibling card.

defects.section: Source citation below the hero image (V3SourceLine)
defects.finding: "Source: live MLS through Ore..." is clipped by the left edge of the viewport at 1440px and by the right edge at 375px in both shots — the citation is unreadable in its entirety on both breakpoints.
defects.primitive: components/site/v3/V3SourceLine.tsx (shared primitive — this defect ships on every page that uses it)
defects.fix: Constrain the source line to the content column's measure instead of a margin/gutter position that falls outside the viewport.

defects.finding: The only data display in the first viewport is a photo-price-badge-address card, identical in form to a portal's price-reduced search results. There is no distribution of the 60 cuts, no sparkline of the price history, nothing that turns the count into a picture — a reader would not screenshot this to show someone.
defects.fix: Put a claim-first drawing above the grid — a dot-strip of the 60 cuts by size, hover reveals address and percent — so the page shows something a portal feed does not before it hands off to the card list.

defects.section: Hero stat line ("60 price cuts this week · 48 shown below")
defects.finding: The one figure on the page is static text with no hover, toggle, or drill-in — no way to see the breakdown by city or cut size without reading every card below.
defects.fix: Make the count answer a question on interaction — a small toggle by city or by cut-size band that re-filters the grid below it.

rows.dullest: The listing grid itself, even setting the overlap bug aside — it is a photo, a price, a badge, and an address, the exact form of a portal's price-reduced search results, with no chart or drill-in to make the reader pause.
rows.verdict: The masthead is on-brand, but directly beneath it the email-signup card overlaps and hides listing prices and addresses on both desktop and mobile, and the grid underneath is a plain portal-style card list with no interaction — this currently loses to a working Redfin price-cut search page on legibility alone.

rows.beats: no win named — the visible fold has no photograph, no team imagery, and no data depth; a comparable Central Oregon brokerage about page (Cascade Sotheby's International Realty – Bend, or Windermere Central Oregon's about/team page) opens with office or team photography and structured bios, which this fold does not have to counter with

defects.finding: Below the Amboqia H1 and one-line description, the entire remaining fold at both viewports is seven identical hairline-divided link rows — Principal broker, Call, Text, Email, Schedule, Client reviews, Contact — each just text plus a trailing arrow glyph, with no photo, mark, or map anywhere in view.
defects.fix: Give the hero band a visual anchor (an office/team photo, not only text) and differentiate the contact channels by form (icon system, grouped tap targets) instead of one repeating row shape.

defects.finding: None of the seven rows rewards a hover, tap, or scrub with more information — each is a bare anchor to tel:/sms:/mailto:/route href, so the section's only 'interaction' is leaving the page.
defects.fix: Turn at least one row into a real interaction that reveals data in place — e.g. 'Client reviews' expanding to show the live average and count on hover before the reader commits to leaving the page — rather than every row being a plain link-out.

defects.finding: Seven text rows with no visual encoding (no mark, bar, image, or map) is exactly the banned tell 'scrolling lists as the design' — a table wearing hairlines — applied here to a link menu instead of a data ledger.
defects.fix: Encode the channels visually (icon-per-channel, grouped 2-up tiles, or a single expanding 'reach a broker' control) instead of a flat vertical list of anchors.

defects.finding: At 375px the license row plus seven link rows consume the entire viewport with no visual cue that Proof, Firm closings, broker Faces, and Atlas exist further down — the mobile fold reads as a complete, finished (and empty) page.
defects.fix: Compress the contact rows into a denser 2-up icon grid on mobile so the fold reaches a differentiator (a face, a figure, a map) sooner.

rows.dullest: The #who contact-link stack — it is a column of seven anchor tags with an arrow icon, no image, no data mark, nothing that earns a second look before the reader either clicks a phone number or leaves.
tells: Scrolling lists as the design — the seven-row contact list under #who has no visual encoding (no mark, bar, map, or image), which is 'a table wearing hairlines' per TASTE.md, applied to a link menu
rows.verdict: The About page's first screen is a phone book, not a proof point — it opens as a stack of plain contact links with no photo or figure, while the page's actual assets (broker faces, firm sales, reviews, the service-area map) sit entirely below the fold captured here.

defects.finding: The entire first viewport, desktop and mobile, is 16 flat number+label tiles in a 4-column grid — months of supply, active listings, median list price, days to offer, etc. — with no chart, bar, sparkline, or map anywhere on screen. Every tile is the same visual weight and the same treatment repeated 16 times: a number, then jargon underneath it.
defects.fix: Cap the headline figure row at 3-4 figures with a plain sentence per figure, and promote the region chart (already wired as the `chart` prop but pushed off-screen by the tile count) into the fold — a hero figure or a stat tile with a sparkline for months of supply, per the dataviz house preference order, not a 16-up grid.

defects.finding: Nothing in the visible viewport responds to hover, tap, scrub, or toggle. `annualCharts.region` is passed into this same component, so an interactive chart exists in the code, but the 16-tile figures row is tall enough to push it entirely below the fold on both 1440 and 375 shots — the one interactive element on the page's opening section is invisible on load.
defects.fix: Reorder so the chart renders beside or above the figure row, not after it, so the interactive element is inside the first viewport instead of buried under two rows of static tiles.

defects.finding: The visible shape is eyebrow ("CENTRAL OREGON ANNUAL REVIEW") → Amboqia headline → hairline rule → rows of figures — the exact template shape TASTE.md names as the model's "statistically safest layout" to avoid, reproduced faithfully in navy-on-cream rather than avoided.
defects.fix: Break the internal rhythm of the primitive itself for a figure count this high: something other than eyebrow→heading→rule→grid has to carry the open, e.g. the chart or a two-bar MOS drawing sits where the grid currently opens the section.

defects.finding: At 375px the viewport shows six tiles and cuts the seventh row mid-figure ("5,770" / "46.3%" clipped at the bottom edge) with no visual signal that content continues — the phone's entire first screen is numbers with no photo, map, or color break to relieve it.
defects.fix: At narrow widths, either scroll-snap the figure grid as its own contained region with a visible "more" affordance, or drop to the capped 3-4 headline figures so the fold doesn't end mid-tile.

tells: "KPI grids." — "A number, a percentage, and jargon" — a figure with no plain sentence beside it saying what it means for the reader. Present across the entire opening #market Instrument: 16 tiles, each a number over a small-caps label, no interpretive sentence.

"The stacked-section page." — eyebrow → heading → rows → source. The opening section alone reproduces this shape (eyebrow, Amboqia H1, hairline rule, figure rows) even before any second section is counted.
rows.beats: no win named — as captured, the fold shows a static 16-tile grid with no visible chart or interaction; a comparable portal market-data page (e.g. Redfin's city housing-market page) pairs the same category of stats with an interactive hover chart in the same viewport, so no metric in what's visible here is a win
rows.dullest: The opening #market section, which is the entire visible page on both shots — 16 static stat tiles with zero chart, mark, or interactive element in view; a reader scrolls past it the way they'd scroll past a spreadsheet, and the wired chart that could have carried the section never appears in the fold.
rows.verdict: The annual review opens with sixteen flat stat tiles and no visible chart on either desktop or phone — it reads as a spreadsheet pasted onto the brand colors, not the market page built to out-class a portal's.

defects.section: map pane (right pane desktop / full-bleed mobile)
defects.finding: The basemap is stock, unstyled Google Maps — Google's own terrain greens/tans, road line weights, place-label typography, plus Google's default UI chrome (Map/Satellite toggle, +/- zoom buttons, attribution). This is the exact object TASTE.md names by example as banned for a data surface ('Not a Google default map'). It breaks the two-color navy-on-cream system across roughly 55% of the desktop viewport and 70% of the mobile viewport — the single largest area on the page carries none of the brand.
defects.fix: Restyle the basemap to Atlas-grade cartography — navy line work and cream ground matching V3Atlas's map object — so the pins, roads, and labels read as one composed brand surface instead of a third-party widget with brand-colored stickers on top.

defects.section: map pin cluster, center of the desktop map (Tetherow / SW Bend / Mountain View area)
defects.finding: A dense cluster of price/count pins (13, 17, 18, 7, 22, 28, 25, 6, 9, 39, 90...) stack directly on top of each other with no collapse behavior, producing a patch of overlapping navy circles where individual values are unreadable.
defects.fix: Replace raw per-listing pin stacking with a zoom-aware cluster badge that merges overlapping markers into one grouped count and expands on hover or zoom-in, rather than letting markers collide.

defects.section: map pins near the viewport edge (top-right, right edge)
defects.finding: Several price badges (e.g. the cluster near '42', '$625k', the right-edge '8' and '12' badges) are sliced by the frame edge, reading as a broken/clipped element rather than an intentional map pan.
defects.fix: Pad the initial map fit-bounds so no marker's full badge sits within its own width of the viewport edge on load.

defects.section: whole page composition (filter dock + list rail + map)
defects.finding: The page is the unmodified split list+map real-estate-portal layout — same card-list-left/map-right structure, same filter-pill row, same card format as Zillow, Redfin, and Realtor.com. Nothing here is a compositional choice a template would not make; there is no claim-first framing anywhere ('X homes, priced Y–Z, in this view') tying the list and map together as one authored object.
defects.primitive: app/search/page.tsx (composes SearchFilters + SearchResults + MapSearchView with no shared framing element)
defects.fix: Add a thin editorial header above the results rail stating the claim for the current view (count, price range, place) so the list+map reads as one composed data object rather than two bolted-together portal widgets.

defects.section: results list rail (left column cards, desktop; list state, mobile)
defects.finding: Cards are photo + price + beds/baths/sqft + address — identical in form to every incumbent portal's result card. There is no encoded comparison signal (no price/sqft percentile mark, no DOM indicator relative to the visible map set), so scanning the list gives no more than the raw facts already on each card.
defects.fix: Encode one comparative signal directly on the card row — a thin price/sqft position mark against the visible result set — so the list rewards scanning with a read the raw numbers alone don't give.

defects.section: filter bar (PLACES / FOR SALE / PRICE / BEDS / BATHS / HOME TYPE / ALL FILTERS / SAVE THIS SEARCH)
defects.finding: Seven uniform pill buttons in a single row with no weight hierarchy — Price, the filter buyers touch most, reads with the same visual weight as School District or Save Search.
defects.fix: Give the highest-use filters (Price, Beds/Baths) more visual weight than the rest instead of a uniform pill row.

tells: Not a Google default map — the map pane is unstyled stock Google Maps cartography and chrome, the exact thing TASTE.md's binding ritual names as banned for a data surface

Card grids / list-as-design chrome shared with every portal, with no compositional choice distinguishing it (borderline the 'scrolling lists as the design' tell — mitigated only by the presence of photos, so not a strict hit, but the same generic effect)
rows.beats: No win named. The page is structurally identical to Zillow's and Redfin's map-search UX (split list+map, same filter row, same card format), and its basemap — unstyled Google Maps chrome — reads less finished than Redfin's custom-styled map. Per TASTE.md rule 7, if no win can be named the section is not done; none is named here.
rows.dullest: The map basemap: stock, unstyled Google Maps cartography occupying the majority of both viewports, carrying none of the site's navy-on-cream identity.
rows.verdict: This is a correctly-functioning, well-engineered search page (real viewport sync, draw tool, degraded-state handling, registry-driven filters — the honesty/function criterion is the strongest score here) wearing the single most generic layout in real estate: the unmodified Zillow/Redfin split list+map, with an unstyled third-party Google basemap dominating most of the screen. It is the textbook 'distributional convergence' failure TASTE.md describes — safest layout, correct every time, identical to every incumbent, and specifically the exact object ('a Google default map') the canon names as banned. Median score 32/100 reflects a page that is functional and clean but has made no composed, brand-authored choice anywhere a reader would screenshot.

rows.beats: No win named. A Zillow or Redfin ZIP-code search results page (map + card list) is the closest comparable, and on this evidence it is not clearly beaten: their maps are also default-styled but their card lists carry saved-search and comparison affordances this page's cards do not show above the fold.

defects.section: Field (map + list, no visible id — first section under the H1)
defects.finding: The map is a stock Google Maps embed: tan/gray default roadmap tiles, the blue 'Google' wordmark, the standard white zoom +/- stack and a 'Map ▾' type-switcher, all rendered in Google's own visual language, not navy-on-cream. It sits in the primary above-the-fold position on both desktop and mobile.
defects.primitive: app/central-oregon/_v3/PlaceFieldMap.client.tsx (+ PlaceFieldMapImpl.tsx), reused by ZipHomesField via V3Field's mapSlot

defects.finding: Nothing in the visible viewport rewards a hover, tap, or toggle with more data beyond the map's own native pan/zoom (which is Google's interaction, not the page's). No pin-to-card linkage, filter, or segment control is visible above the fold on either breakpoint.
defects.fix: Make map pins and list rows a bound pair the reader can drive: hover a card to highlight its pin, click a pin to scroll/expand its card, and surface a property-type or price-tier toggle in the Field itself rather than only downstream in the market Instrument section.

defects.section: H1 / Field headline ("Homes for sale in 97702")

The only data-first line on screen ('380 active single-family listings in 97702 · the 24 highest-priced below') is a small gray caption under the map, not a headline claim, so the page opens as directory chrome rather than an editorial statement about this ZIP.
defects.fix: Promote a one-sentence, sourced claim into the Field's headline register (e.g. a verdict or trend line drawn from the market Instrument's own trace) so the first read lands a point, not just a label plus a caption.

defects.finding: The card list is the standard portal pattern verbatim: photo left, price/address/beds-baths-sqft/subdivision right, undifferentiated rows. It is not a bare text ledger (it carries images), but it makes no deliberate choice a template would not make, and nothing in the visible four rows groups, encodes, or ranks by anything beyond price order.
defects.primitive: components/site/v3 V3Field row rendering, called from app/zip/[zip]/_v3/ZipHomesField.tsx
defects.fix: Give the row list a house move — e.g. a subdivision-grouped rail, a visual price-tier marker, or a compact sparkline/segment strip per row — so the list itself, not just the map, carries a Ryan Realty-specific form.

rows.dullest: The Field/map section: the map is the visual centerpiece of the first viewport and it is an unstyled, default Google Maps embed with Google's own chrome — the exact object TASTE.md names as the thing not to ship ("Not a Google default map"). I would not stop scrolling on the strength of what's visible; the page reads as a functional listings directory, not an editorial statement about this ZIP.
tells: Not a Google default map — the Field's map is a real stock Google Maps embed with default tan/gray tiles, the Google wordmark, and default zoom/type controls, occupying roughly half the primary viewport on both desktop and mobile.

KPI grids (partial) — the one data-first line present ('380 active single-family listings...') is a bare caption with no plain-sentence framing of what it means for the reader, closer to a number-plus-jargon fragment than a claim.
rows.verdict: The page functions and the typography/layout outside the map is on-brand, but the hero section is a default Google Maps embed next to a stock portal-style card list, so the first thing a visitor sees is the exact pattern TASTE.md forbids, not a Ryan Realty original.

rows.beats: Cascade Sotheby's International Realty's Bend agent directory — each agent card opens into a bio, specialty areas, and that broker's actual sold/active listings; Ryan Realty's /team gives a headshot, a license number, and four contact buttons with no path into any broker's actual work.

defects.finding: Nothing on the page rewards a hover, tap, scrub, or toggle with more information. The four buttons per card (Call/Text/Email/Schedule) are exit actions, not reveals — the page has zero data interaction, failing the rubric's interaction bar outright.

defects.finding: At 1440x900 the entire page — breadcrumb, H1, card grid, footer — fits in one screen with nothing below it worth scrolling to. rows.beats: Redfin's regional Housing Market pages (e.g. redfin.com/city/.../housing-market) open above the fold with a live market-temperature figure and a price chart. rows.dullest: #chooser — a visitor's honest first read of a page titled "housing market" is a five-row text menu with no number, mark, or chart anywhere on screen; nobody stops scrolling here, and there is nothing yet to stop for.

rows.beats: Redfin's Medford, OR page — an interactive map with hover-revealed price markers sits in the first viewport alongside the listing grid, so a reader is already exploring supply geographically before any scroll; Ryan Realty's Medford page shows three static numbers and a button in the same space.

defects.fix: Give the figure row a form, not just values: a small inventory graphic (e.g. a two-bar comparison of active vs. recently closed, per the DATA_GRAPHICS 'MOS is two bars, not a tile that says 3.9' principle) or a one-line claim sentence directly under the figures stating what 725 active / $473K means for a Medford buyer or seller.

defects.finding: Nothing in the entire first viewport rewards a hover, tap, or scrub with more data. The three figures are inert text; only the nav dropdowns and the CTA button respond to input at all.
defects.fix: Make at least one figure interactive — hover a figure to reveal the row count or a mini price distribution, or make the median figure open a scrubbable timeline of recent list-price activity for the city — so the section clears the 'every data section rewards interaction' bar instead of sitting as three static labels.

defects.finding: The hero carries no image, map, or place-specific mark of any kind — nothing ties this screen to Medford rather than any of the ~362 other cities this same template renders. A reader could not screenshot this section to show anyone; it is the template, not the place.
defects.fix: Add one place-anchoring visual element to the class (not a one-off): a small locator mark, a thumbnail from the newest listing's photo, or a compact map chip — something that varies per city and gives the eye somewhere to land before the figure row.

defects.finding: Both sections visible in the shots open with the identical eyebrow-then-serif-heading band, back to back, with no change in width, density, or media between them — the start of the stacked-section rhythm the rubric bans, even though the underlying components differ (Instrument then Quiet).
defects.fix: Vary the visual treatment of the second band even where the component differs underneath — narrower measure, a rule instead of a repeated eyebrow chip, or pull the honest-market prose beside a small map of the service area rather than stacking it under an identical eyebrow-heading header.

tells: KPI grids. "A number, a percentage, and jargon" — a figure with no plain sentence beside it saying what it means for the reader. (present in #top's three-figure row)
rows.dullest: The hero (#top): three static numbers and a button, no image, no map, no interaction, indistinguishable from the same section on any of the other ~360 city pages this route serves — no, a reader would not stop scrolling here.
rows.verdict: A correct, honestly-sourced, gated hero that is still a KPI grid with a button under it — it will not beat a portal's Medford page on the one thing that matters in the first viewport: something to touch.

rows.beats: No win can be named for what is actually in these two shots. The visible content is a full-bleed photo, an eyebrow, a serif headline, and one CTA button — zero data, zero listings, zero map. Zillow's Bend/Central-Oregon search (zillow.com/bend-or/) and Redfin's Bend page both put an interactive map with live pins and a listing grid in the first viewport; a buyer on those sites is looking at real inventory before they scroll once. Ryan Realty's /buy asks the same buyer to click "Search homes" and leave the page before they see a single house. The route file shows a live listings Field (HomeHomesField, with a map slot) sits immediately below this hero — that would be the real answer to "does it beat Zillow" — but it is below the fold in both shots, so it cannot be scored or credited here.
rows.dullest: The hero. Eyebrow ("CENTRAL OREGON") over a large serif headline over one CTA button on a full-bleed landscape photo is the exact shape TASTE.md names as the model's "statistically safest layout" — the only difference from the banned "stacked-section" description is that there is no figure row yet, because there is no data in the hero at all. It is a page whose entire job is helping someone buy a house, and its first and only visible content in a 900px-tall capture is a picture of a mountain.
rows.verdict: Competent, on-brand, and inert. Everything visible reads as Ryan Realty (navy/cream, Amboqia headline, the two-color hairline system) and nothing in the crop breaks a hard rule — no purple gradient, no centered-everything, no off-brand hex. But the entire visible page is a stock real-estate hero: photo, eyebrow, headline, one button. There is no data, no figure, no interactive element, nothing to hover, scrub, or toggle anywhere in either shot. For the one page on the site whose job is to start a home search, showing zero homes above the fold is the honest failure here, and it is a failure of FORM, not brand: the Stage primitive gives every page that uses it the same "click through before you see anything" opening, whether or not that page has live inventory to lead with. The route comment confirms buy has live listings and a map ready one scroll down (HomeHomesField) — that content needs to bleed into the first viewport, not wait for it.
tells: Matches TASTE.md's own description of distributional convergence almost verbatim: eyebrow → heading → CTA, with photo standing in for the missing figure row.

No data, image detail, or interactive element anywhere in the captured viewport at either width — the floor stated by the rubric ("a static figure row is the floor, never the ceiling") is not even reached; there is no figure row at all.
The page's stated job (buy a home) is represented only by a button that says 'Search homes,' i.e. 'go elsewhere to do the actual thing this page is for.'

defects.finding: The hero is a photo + eyebrow + serif headline + single CTA with no data and nothing to interact with — the buy-page equivalent of a wall of text: a wall of atmosphere. A person cannot learn anything about the Central Oregon market or see a single home without leaving this section.
defects.fix: Give Stage on a page with live inventory (buy has buyTiles + buyCities already fetched server-side) a data strip inside the hero itself — a live count ('412 homes for sale right now'), a median price, or a scrub-to-preview of three listings — so the claim of the page lands before the first scroll, not after a click.

defects.finding: The route already fetches live listing tiles and a map-bearing Field component and places it directly under the hero, but the fold cuts it off after roughly 60px of an unlabeled photo strip on desktop and even less on mobile — so the page's actual differentiator (live MLS inventory, a map) reads as an accidental crop, not a section.
defects.fix: Shrink the Stage's vertical footprint (or its overlay/CTA block) so the Field's map or first listing row breaks the fold on a standard 900px viewport — the reader should see at least one house before they stop scrolling.

defects.finding: The 'Search homes' button is a plain cream rectangle with a thin border and black-ish text sitting on a photo — it reads as a generic bordered box, not a considered CTA against the rest of the page's typographic confidence (the Amboqia headline is doing all the design work; the button is doing none).
defects.fix: Give the Stage CTA the same intentionality as the headline — navy fill with cream type (inverted from the current cream-fill/dark-text box) so it reads as the brand's primary action color rather than a neutral form-field-shaped box.

rows.beats: No win named. Zillow's own Tetherow/Bend neighborhood pages already show price-tagged pins on an interactive map plus bed/bath/price filters on the list; this page's Atlas shows bare unlabeled navy dots (no price, no filter) and its list has zero sort/filter, so on the evidence in these two shots it does not clearly beat that portal floor — it matches or trails it. The subject's own site (tetherow.com) still wins on identity/photography; this page has no hero image or lifestyle framing at all in the fold, only the wordmark and a headline.
rows.dullest: Desktop's entire first viewport, below the header and one headline, is eight identical rows of thumbnail–address–price–specs with a hairline between each — no chart, no map, no claim sentence, no visual encoding of price. It is the rubric's own definition of a banned tell ("a Ledger past six rows with no visual encoding is a table wearing hairlines"), and on desktop it is not one section among several, it IS the fold.
rows.verdict: Fails the standard. The mobile fold at least shows the class's differentiator (V3Atlas, cream field / navy marks / boundary polygon) before the list, which is the right idea half-executed (no price on pins, no visible interaction, undersized zoom controls). The desktop fold shows none of that — the atlas section is entirely absent, leaving a raw scrolling address list as the whole first impression, which is exactly the "wall of text, scrolling lists, boring" pattern this rubric exists to kill. Because the same page renders two different section orders/contents across the two shots, the likely cause is the boundary fetch's silent timeout fallback (4500ms, falls back to a null polygon) rather than a deliberate design — that makes this an honesty/function defect on top of a design one: the page's differentiator is not guaranteed to render.
tells: Scrolling lists as the design — a same-shape row repeated 8+ times with no visual encoding of price, the exact banned tell
Missing states — the Atlas/differentiator section renders on mobile's capture but is entirely absent from desktop's capture of the same URL, i.e. a display that only renders on some loads
No claim-first sentence — the H1 is a label ('Single-family in Tetherow'), not a plain-language claim with a figure, violating TASTE's first test
Sub-44px tap targets on the mobile map's zoom +/- controls

defects.finding: The entire desktop first viewport below the H1 is a raw, repeated list of listing rows (thumbnail, address, price, specs) with no chart, map, stat, or claim sentence — literally the 'scrolling lists as the design' banned tell, and here it is not a section, it is the whole fold.

defects.finding: The Atlas (the class's stated differentiator) appears on mobile's capture directly under the H1 but is completely absent from desktop's capture of the identical URL — its render is gated on a boundary fetch with a 4500ms timeout that silently falls back to a null polygon, dropping the whole section with no placeholder.
defects.primitive: atlasRegions.length > 0 ? <V3Atlas .../> : null gate in app/communities/[slug]/types/[type]/page.tsx, fed by getGeoBoundaryMapData / getResortBoundaryGeoJSON via withTimeoutFallback(Result)
defects.fix: Never silently drop the differentiator section — stream in a lightweight skeleton/placeholder while the boundary resolves (or budget more time for this specific call) so Atlas is present on every load, not a race outcome.

TASTE's own first test — 'what is this section's claim, stated in one plain sentence' — fails: there is no figure (count, median price, price band) stated in language before the reader has to parse the list or map themselves.
defects.fix: Add a one-line, §0-sourced claim under the H1, e.g. '14 single-family homes for sale in Tetherow, $1.35M–$4.25M' — the page already computes hud/segment counts, it just never prints them as a sentence.

defects.finding: The list and the map show the same listings but are not connected — no hover-on-row highlights the matching Atlas dot (or vice versa), no sort or filter (price, beds) sits above the list. defects.fix: Wire row hover/tap to highlight the corresponding Atlas pin and vice versa; add a lightweight price/bed sort or filter control above the list so the section rewards interaction rather than just navigation.

defects.finding: Thumbnails (~64px) are inconsistently cropped — aerial, interior, and exterior-at-dusk photos are all forced into the same small square with no visual encoding of price or standout status, reinforcing the 'table wearing hairlines' read once past six rows.
defects.fix: Either encode price visually (size/emphasis banding) or cap the raw row list and move the remainder into a richer, map-linked view instead of one more identical row.

defects.finding: A blank band of roughly 160px sits between the breadcrumb and the first content block on both desktop and mobile, with no image, mark, or headline anchoring it — reads as a missing hero or a layout gap rather than deliberate breathing room.

defects.fix: Merge the reach strip into the V3Proof hero band (e.g., as a slim action row directly under the claim sentence) so the opening reads as one composed hero rather than two stacked sections handing off to each other.

defects.finding: None of the five stat tiles invite a hover, tap, or reveal in the captured viewport on either device — the only interaction on the page (a hoverable month-by-month review timeline, per the sentence 'Point at a mark to read it, or pick a year' cut off at the bottom of the desktop shot) sits entirely below the fold, so the first screen a visitor sees is fully static.

rows.beats: no win named — did not browse a live competing brokerage or portal contact page this pass, and TASTE.md forbids inventing one. On the shots alone this page does not obviously clear a typical brokerage contact page: no map, no photo, no live availability/booking state, and a four-times-repeated identical card row that most competitor contact pages also default to.

defects.fix: Give the row a live state instead of four static links — an on-duty/response-time indicator that updates a card's content, or one dominant primary action plus three lighter secondary links — so the four cells stop reading as an interchangeable stat-tile grid.

defects.finding: The first viewport is pure type on cream — eyebrow, Amboqia headline, one paragraph, an address line — no photo, mark, or map. defects.fix: Break the column with one non-type element in the hero — a stripped office-location mark, a small broker photo, or a single interactive element — so the page does not open as consecutive hairline text rows at either viewport.

defects.finding: Four equal-width bordered cells each carrying an arrow icon is the silhouette of the banned 'card grid with icons' tell, even though each caption sentence keeps it just short of the literal KPI-grid definition (a figure with no sentence).

defects.finding: No image, mark, or visual element departs from navy-on-cream text anywhere in the captured fold at either 1440 or 375 — restraint has tipped into a page with nothing to look at besides paragraphs and a phone number.
defects.fix: Introduce one navy-on-cream graphic element (not a photo, not a new hue) that gives the eye something besides type before the reader has to scroll for it.

rows.verdict: The hero chart is on-brand and reads clean, but the only section visible in the fold ships a garbled, jargon-leaking source citation and a database-count disclosure label, and shows one metric where the standard calls for a breathtaking, multi-object region report.

rows.beats: Redfin's "Bend, OR Single-Family Homes for Sale" map/list page (flat pin cluster on a Google-style basemap, no density encoding, no recent-activity feed): Ryan Realty's Atlas wins on data depth (a sale-density heatmap by micro-area, not just pins) and freshness (a live just-listed/went-pending/sold ticker with a timestamp). It does not beat Redfin on stating the market's point — Redfin's page at least implies its claim through sort order; this page states no claim sentence at all.

defects.finding: Two near-duplicate Amboqia display headlines stack with only whitespace between them: the page H1 'Single-family in Bend' is immediately followed by V3Atlas's own heading 'Single-family on the map'. The top of the page says the same thing twice instead of making a claim.
defects.primitive: app/cities/[slug]/types/[type]/page.tsx (the headline passed into V3Atlas at the atlasRegions block, built from placeTypeHeadline/atlasViewForType in @/lib/place/place-type-page); V3Atlas in components/site/v3 has no compact/eyebrow mode for when it directly follows the page H1

defects.finding: No plain-language claim sentence appears anywhere above the fold. The reader sees a title, a control rail, and a map, but never a sentence stating what the map shows about single-family homes in Bend — no concentration, price band, or pace claim.
defects.fix: Add one sentence of narrative copy under the H1, drawn from the pace/segment data already fetched in the loader (getPublicDetachedPace / getPublicPlaceSegments), stating the section's claim before the figures.

defects.finding: Four different control idioms — gradient swatch legend, dot legend, a checkbox, and a slider — plus a three-line recent-activity ticker are stacked with spacing alone as the separator. No divider or sub-heading groups them, so the rail reads as a dense instrument panel rather than an edited, editorial rail.
defects.primitive: V3Atlas (components/site/v3) — owns the legend/filter rail markup
defects.fix: Group the rail into two blocks (map legend vs. filter controls) separated by a hairline rule, each carrying a small label, so the rail has the same one-rhythm discipline as the rest of the page.

defects.finding: The listings ledger — the page's only other section — is a sliver at the very bottom of the desktop shot and invisible on mobile. A tall opening (duplicate headline plus a full-height map) pushes the second section out of the first scroll entirely on a phone.

defects.fix: Shrink the opening's vertical footprint by fixing the duplicate-headline defect, so the listings ledger surfaces within or near the first scroll on mobile.

tells: No literal named banned tell (walls-of-text, scrolling-list-as-design, KPI grid, purple gradient, card-grid-with-icons, frosted glass, emoji, hover bounce) is present — the rail avoids KPI-tile jargon entirely, matching the page's own comment 'Do not print leftover KPIs on the opening.'
Construction-not-composition (TASTE's own diagnosis #3): the H1 and the Atlas's internal heading were built as two separate components and glued together rather than composed as one opening moment.
Claim-first ritual question 1 unmet: no plain sentence states the section's point anywhere above the fold.
rows.dullest: The opening: two near-identical Amboqia headlines ("Single-family in Bend" then "Single-family on the map") stacked with nothing but whitespace between them. It is the single least-composed passage on the page, made worse by sitting directly above a genuinely strong object — the Atlas density map — that TASTE itself names as the reference to copy.
rows.verdict: The core object is right: V3Atlas's density heatmap, dot legend, type toggle, price slider, and live activity ticker is exactly the interactive, data-first object TASTE.md holds up as the standard, and it beats a flat portal pin-map on depth and freshness. But the page opens with a duplicated headline instead of a claim, the control rail crams four idioms together with no grouping, and the page's only other section (photographed listings) is pushed almost entirely below the fold, especially on mobile. Correct, gated, and carrying a strong reference primitive, but the opening third of the page is unfinished composition, not a finished editorial moment.
